blocks.content: The National Green Tribunal is mandated to make an endeavor for disposal of applications or appeals finally within six months of filing.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established under the NGT Act 2010 for effective and expeditious disposal of environmental disputes.
Persistent vacancies in judicial and expert member posts hamper the functioning and cause a backlog of cases.
The lack of financial autonomy restricts operational independence as NGT relies on the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
Jurisdictional overlaps arise due to frequent constitutional challenges against NGT orders in High Courts under Article 226.
Enforcement of NGT orders remains a key bottleneck due to dependency on state authorities and local administration.
NGT is bound by principles of Natural Justice and is NOT bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
An appeal against any order/decision of NGT lies directly to the Supreme Court within 90 days.
The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 and Forest Rights Act, 2006 are explicitly excluded from NGT's jurisdiction.
